What you’ll need (free) - A computer with a modern browser (Chrome/Firefox). - A code editor (VS Code, Sublime, or similar). - Python 3 installed (for a simple local server) or Node.js if you prefer. - Optionally: Git for version control. Step 1 — Create a simple static website 1. Make a project folder (e.g., demo-site). 2. Inside it create index.html, styles.css, and script.js. index.html (simple, harmless login form for demonstration) Demo Login

styles.css (basic styling) body { font-family: Arial, sans-serif; padding: 20px; } label { display: inline-block; width: 80px; } input { margin-bottom: 10px; } script.js (client-side demo behavior only; do NOT send credentials anywhere) document.getElementById('loginForm').addEventListener('submit', function(e) { e.preventDefault(); // For learning only: show a message instead of submitting credentials. alert('This is a local demo. No credentials are sent anywhere.'); }); Step 2 — Serve the site locally - Using Python 3: open a terminal in the project folder and run: python -m http.server 8000 - Open http://localhost:8000 in your browser. Never target real users or services. Further learning resources - OWASP Web Security Testing Guide: https://owasp.org - MDN Web Docs (HTML/CSS/JS): https://developer.mozilla.org - Guides on secure authentication and password storage.
